description: A person's acknowledgment of one revision of a policy. It has person or person_match, or both; a reader shows one with neither, or whose match finds no one or several people, as unresolved.

method.description: How the person signed in to acknowledge.

person.description: When the person travels in the same bundle.

person_match.description: Who acknowledged, for a reader to match. Needs emails or identifiers.

policy.description: The policy, a tech.monorail.policy.document, with revision and sha256 (its content hash) pinning the exact text acknowledged.

signature.description: The acknowledging system's own signature over this record, beside any bundle signature. Ed25519 over "tech.monorail.policy.acknowledgment v1" and a newline, then the record's content line without the signature field - its canonical line without produced_by, source and the final newline (records.md § Content lines) - by the key named here in that publisher's key set. Republishing the record with new provenance keeps it valid. A key retired before the acknowledgment's at doesn't count. A signature is evidence only when its publisher is one the reader already trusts to attest acknowledgments, normally the policy's publisher or the bundle's signer; any other is shown as unverified, as is one that fails to verify or has an alg other than ed25519. A failed signature never makes a bundle bad_bundle.

key.description: The key's id in that key set.

publisher.description: Whose key set holds the key.

value.description: The 64-byte signature, in canonical base64url without padding.

source_fields.description: The source's own fields that no field here covers, under the source's names. Readers keep it and don't interpret it. Never a personal value that a field here would label.

statement.description: The words they agreed to, when not just "I have read and agree".

title: policy-acknowledgment
